_schema: THE CHAPTER SCRIPT, as data. public/js/story_runtime.js reads this and owns no line, no flag name, no coordinate and no camera id of its own — adding a beat is an edit HERE, never a code change. FIELDS. beats[]: {id, chapter, scene, cam, at:[x,y,z], r, vTol, when, once, do[]}. A beat fires on the physics tick when EVERY stated trigger holds: `scene` is the scenegraph node, `cam` the baked shot that must be up, `at`+`r` a proximity circle in runtime coords, `when` a condition in dialogue.js's OWN language (flag/notFlag/flagIs/flagAtLeast/hasItem/goldAtLeast/all/any/not — there is exactly one condition language in this project). `once` defaults true and is ledgered in GS.state.beats, i.e. IN THE SAVE, so a reload cannot replay a cutscene. do[] steps: {dialogue:id} plays a node from `nodes` below through the ordinary dialogue window; {setFlags}/{incFlags}/{giveItem,qty}/{gold} go through GS and nowhere else; {objective}/{banner}/{toast}/{endCard}/{wait}/{shot}/{chapter}/{save} are presentation. THERE IS NO TELEPORT STEP, on purpose: a beat never moves the player across a scene, because the corridor between the towns is WALKED (chapter2.js:261 fakes it with a fade and a coordinate; that is the anti-pattern this layer retires). nodes/speakers: injected into dialogue.js at load (Dialogue.inject) — the story does not get a second renderer.
_provenance: Chapters One and Two ONLY (user scope ruling 2026-08-02); chapter3.js is out of scope and Chapter Two's end card is TERMINAL. Beat staging follows docs/plans/ch1-staging-audit.md's beat table against the ratified Emberbrook map; the flag contract is docs/plans/end-to-end-wiring.md §6. Prose is lifted from the SHIPPED public/js/chapter1.js and chapter2.js, condensed — those files were rewritten to docs/VOICES.md at HEAD 2e4e461, so the voice is the ratified one and no line here is newly invented dialogue.
_twoPlayerPending: THE 3D RUNTIME IS SINGLE-BODY and the user has NOT yet ruled on co-op (end-to-end-wiring R1: build two bodies / re-stage with Lake as an AI companion / ship single-player). Chapter One's climax is two keepers on twin sigil plates and Chapter Two's is a six-hand winch. Both are staged here so ONE player can complete them, with Lake acting as a companion who takes the far plate and the far bar himself. Every such site is marked TWO-PLAYER PENDING in the node it lives in. Nothing here soft-locks in either world: if a second body lands, these beats become two-actor by adding a hold step, not by rewriting the chapter.

On the grey road north, theirs was the last light walking.

lines: The current took the little boat the moment it felt her — north, quick and cold.
Down the water her father drew wrong, and her mother let her go to fix.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: On the last night of autumn, a mapmaker walked into a valley that was not on any of her maps.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (Eleven days out of Harrowmere. Two of them on a road my own survey says is a river.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (There are lights up ahead. Lights mean somebody who can tell me where I am.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (A waystone. Good — the road's a real road, then.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (…Wait.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (I've drawn this stone. This exact stone — the face, the crack through its chin.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (It's in my sketchbook right now. And I have never been here in my life.)

lines.speaker: mochi
lines.text: Mrrp.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: GAH— …a cat. Hello. Don't sneak up on people in haunted forests.

lines.speaker: mochi
lines.text: Mrrp.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: There are lights up the road. Come on. If anyone can explain my sketchbook, it's whoever lives here.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: The wood thinned, and there was an arch with harvest wreaths on it, and past the arch a square full of lamplight and people.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (A festival. Of course. I arrive somewhere for the first time in my life and it's the one night they're all outside.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (That warmth is not weather. I have been cold for eleven days and I stopped being cold at the arch.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (Right. Somebody here knows what a gate on my chart is doing in a valley that isn't.)

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Now then! A guest, and on Emberwake of all nights. Welcome, my dear.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Vesper. Mapmaker. I need to get through your gate, and I'm told you're in charge.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: In charge! Ha! I keep the ledger; the village keeps itself.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: And nobody opens the Old Gate, child. It hasn't a key — it has RULES.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Rules can be charted. Charting things is my whole profession.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: …Ha! I like you. Stay the night, then — and stay for the Kindling Hour.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Three hundred years that flame has burned. In all of them, nobody here carried a grief alone.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: That is not boasting, my dear. It is bookkeeping — I checked.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: As for the Gate — lamplighter business, child. His order built it, his order shut it.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Ask HIM. The quiet one with the flame that never goes out.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: You'll find him somewhere across the village, apologizing to lamps.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Apologizing to lamps.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Ha! You'll see.

story.ch1.meet._note: Act II in the shipped script is LAKE'S OWN ACT — player two rises from his grandmother's table, takes her hand-lamp off the hook and walks the rounds. TWO-PLAYER PENDING: the 3D runtime is single-body, so the rounds are re-staged as Vesper finding him mid-round on the pond lane and walking the rest of them with him. Every line below is his; nothing of his act is cut, only its camera. If a second body lands, this beat splits at the meet and Act II becomes playable as authored.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: Down on the pond lane a young man was standing under a dark lamp with a brass lighter in his hand, saying something to it.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Excuse me. You look official — you're holding fire.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Are you the lamplighter, or do I keep collecting cats until one talks?

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Oh. Um. Yes? The first one. Lake. The cats don't talk, to my knowledge.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Vesper. Mapmaker.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: I know. Poppy's told half the square about you.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Your elder says the Old Gate is your family's business, and I need it open.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: The— nobody crosses the Gate. It hasn't opened in my lifetime.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Because this valley isn't on any chart I own. And I walked here anyway.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Something on the other side of that gate has been sending me MAIL, Lake. I intend to answer it in person.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: …what?

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Ask me after. Three lamps left, and the ring closes before full dark — that's the order she gave me.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: (One. While this lamp burns, every house on the lane sits inside the village's heart. Dark lamp, dull street.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: …You're apologizing to it.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: It's been a long year for the lane.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Two more, up in the square. Walk with me.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: (Two. “Light them like you mean it,” she said, “or they gutter by midnight.”)

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: (She never once explained what the meaning involved. I improvise.)

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: (Three. The ring is closed before full dark, same as every night of my life.)

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: (A lit lamp near every door. Now the Hour can start.)

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: The HOUR! Gather, neighbors — to the square!

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Lake — the flame.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Neighbors! The year turns!

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Three hundred years, and the warmth of every one of them — right here.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: You know the trade. Bring the year's best, and tell it to the flame.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: You keep the memory — every minute, yours till you die. The flame keeps the WARMTH, and shines it on all of us, for good.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Who brings the first memory?

lines.speaker: poppy
lines.text: The flood! The spring flood — the whole town in my bakery, bailing water with soup pots, and LAUGHING, gods help us—

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: This is the BEST night.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: …Why did the music stop?

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: It did not happen slowly. Between one heartbeat and the next, the light of Emberbrook — three hundred years of it — stood up and left.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: Moths came off the Heartlight the way sparks come off a struck flint, and did not climb, and did not go anywhere.

lines.speaker: poppy
lines.text: …My stall. My bread. Why doesn't any of it feel like MINE?

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Mama?

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: …I'm sorry — whose child— no. I know whose. Mine.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: I can say it, and it weighs NOTHING— someone's crying. Why is someone crying?

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Mama. It's me, it's Pip. You KNOW me!

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Everyone stay where you are. Names! Say your names, out loud — say them NOW.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: …I know my name. It just doesn't feel like mine to say.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Rowan. Your name is Rowan.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: …You know them? All of them?

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Every window in this village. Every name behind it.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: You two. The stranger and the lamplighter. Everyone in this square is a stranger wearing a neighbor's face — except you.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: I got here an HOUR ago.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: And keepers don't make tellings. We keep our own — Grandmother's one hard rule.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: …My lighter's still warm. Every other flame in Emberbrook just died — not this one.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Then we are not finished. Not yet.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: See to them — all of them. They deserve their names back, even borrowed.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Then come find me. I will be with my ledger — every word of it true, and not one of them mine.

lines.speaker: poppy
lines.text: …My stall. My bread. My hands — I know every burn scar on them. Why does none of it feel like MINE?

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: You're Poppy. You bake.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Every morning you burn your thumb on the first tray, and swear you won't tomorrow.

lines.speaker: poppy
lines.text: …Do I do it anyway?

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Every morning.

lines.speaker: poppy
lines.text: The round warm things. I know the word — it just sounds like nobody's when I say it.

lines.speaker: poppy
lines.text: Say it to me, love.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Honeybuns.

lines.speaker: poppy
lines.text: HONEYBUNS. Say more words. Both of you.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: I'm writing this down. All of it — who you are, and who you are to each other.

lines.speaker: poppy
lines.text: Good, love. Write the thumb. The thumb feels true.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Tell her. TELL her!

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Mara. This is Pip. Your son, seven years old.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: You waited out a snowstorm at the pass for him to be born.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: I believe you. That is the worst of it — every word lands like a fact about a stranger.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: …You held my hand. TONIGHT. You said I'd remember tonight forever.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Pip. Look at me. I saw her holding your hand — an hour ago, by the stall.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: I'm a mapmaker. I keep records of true things.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: So I am telling you: it is TRUE.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: It happened, and I have it.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: …Is it in ink?

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: It is now.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Whoever you two are — whatever you still carry — do not waste it. Please.

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: My name… I can say the word, friend. It just isn't MINE anymore.

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: Hands still know the knots, though. Funny what stays.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Finn. You're Finn.

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: …Finn. Huh. Short. I like it.

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: One thing for your book, mapmaker. The fish stopped circlin' the moment it happened.

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: Like they'd been countin' down to it.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Fish don't count.

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: Didn't think so either. This morning I was wrong about a lot of things.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: The cat. The cat is FINE?!

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (Mochi is purring. Mochi has, if anything, improved.)

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Cats don't keep their hearts where moths can reach. My grandmother used to say that.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Your grandmother said that. Casually. As common knowledge.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: She said a lot of things. She was a lamplighter too.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (He is watching the north road. He does not usually watch anything.)

story.ch1.pact._note: TWO-PLAYER PENDING — the shipped beat ends on `bothHold: HOLD A — swear it together`, two players holding one button. Single-body staging: the oath is one confirmation and Lake speaks his half. The line that carries it is unchanged.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Look at this. The year four-twenty-nine. The flood. A wedding.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: I wrote every line of this page — and tonight I read it like the minutes of somebody else's village.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Ink keeps facts. It cannot keep what they WEIGHED.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Our flame was first drawn from a shrine deep in the Whisperwood. The Kindling.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: And the old Order kept one creed above all: light does not die — it is only ever carried.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Whatever THAT was tonight, it did not put our flame out, children. It carried it off. Whole.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Nobody knows the way. The Gate's been shut three hundred years, and the road's gone.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: …I need to show you both something, and I need you to not be strange about it.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Since I was six years old, I have drawn one clearing. Over and over, in dreams.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Forty-one drawings of the same clearing.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: I came here because the forty-first had YOUR gate in the corner.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Girl… that is the Kindling. That is the heart of the Whisperwood.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: It has been CALLING you. Forty-one times it called.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: The map does not know fire. The flame does not know the way.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: So it must be both of you, together.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: We met an hour ago.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Then you have an hour's head start on resenting each other. Marvelous.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Understand what you carry, boy. That little flame is the last live fire in the valley.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: I'm scared to walk that road, and I'll walk it. Both of those are true.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: The old rite, then. Two keepers, one flame — say it and mean it, or the Gate will know.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: “What they forgot, we keep. What we keep, we return.”

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: What they forgot, we keep. What we keep, we return.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: What they forgot, we keep. What we keep, we return.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: …The cat is going with you.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: He's not my—

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: It was not a question, boy.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: That cat has been watching the north road all evening. Take the hint.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Twin sigils, before the Gate. The Lamplighters cut them, in the old days.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: That road was always meant to be walked by two.

story.ch1.sigils._note: TWO-PLAYER PENDING — the shipped climax is two players standing two plates 510 px apart, both held for 1.2 s (chapter1.js:249-262). Single-body staging: Vesper takes the near plate and LAKE WALKS TO THE FAR ONE HIMSELF as a companion. The plates, the hold and the rite are otherwise unchanged, so a second body turns this back into the authored beat by making his walk a hold.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: The gate court has no lamp. It is the one place in Emberbrook nobody's warmth was ever asked to reach, and tonight that is no longer a distinction.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Two plates. Cut into the road, one either side. Worn smooth.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: The sigils. Grandmother walked me up here once and would not tell me what they were for.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: I'll take the far one. Stand on yours — and don't step off, whatever it does.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (He crosses the court and sets both boots on the far plate. The stone under Vesper warms, slowly, like a hand.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: It's reading us.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Then let it read. What they forgot, we keep.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: Something enormous and patient took its hands off the doors. They came apart at the seam with a sound like a held breath let go.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: …Three hundred years, and it opens like a garden gate.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: It was never locked, Vesper. It was just shut.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (Footsteps on the gate road behind them: Poppy, Mara and Pip, come up from the square to see them off.)

lines.speaker: poppy
lines.text: Take this, love. Nobody leaves Emberbrook hungry — I'm reliably informed that's MY law.

lines.speaker: poppy
lines.text: Honeybuns, a dozen. And the tin comes back, love — that's how I'll know you did.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: It comes back. That's in ink now.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Festival ribbon, from the square. There's no festival to fly it — so take it somewhere that's going somewhere.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: It'll fly, Mara. I'll find it wind.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Wait! I made you a map, and it goes to the MOON.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: You said not yet. So it's for when.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: For the record: this is now the best chart I carry.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Pip, love. Let them walk.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: Beyond the Old Gate, the road ran grey — soft and wrong, like snow that refused to melt, and the whole of it was moths.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: That's where the light went. Some of it never made it to the sky.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (I have wanted an unmapped road my whole life. I imagined it differently.)

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: My grandmother had a saying for the rounds. The first lamp is the whole job — the rest is only more of it.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Then it goes in the book. Come on, partner — first lamp.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: The road left the moths behind somewhere in the second hour, and then the valley simply stopped and went down.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: …That is not on the sheet. That is not on ANY sheet.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: My north chart says gentle fall to marsh. That is a gorge, and there is a town stacked down the inside of it.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (Forty years that sheet has been in print. Somebody drew this from a rumour and everybody after copied him.)

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Vesper.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: On the far bank. The bow — did you see him bow?

lines.speaker: mochi
lines.text: Mrrp.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (Mochi is not purring. Mochi has flattened himself against Vesper's boot and is looking at a place on the opposite wall where nothing is standing.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: …New page. “A hooded man, courteous, on the wrong side of a river.”

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Down, then. Somebody in that town moves boats for a living, and we need to be moved.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: Dellhollow was built the way a stair is built, and it was loudly alive.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: Queues, gulls, a fish auction. And a hundred lanterns never once lit from a Heartlight.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: There's no flame here. Not one.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: And they're — fine. They're better than fine.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: You say that like it's an accusation.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: I say it like a lamplighter who has just found out his whole family's job might have been optional.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Later. River first. Find whoever tells the water what to do.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: Nineteen days, and not one boat through Lock Five. Before you ask: no, and no, and I'll say it again this afternoon.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: We only need to go downstream.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: So does the queue. There is a river-eel nesting on the sluice grate — forty feet of tenant with a lease she wrote herself.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: You do not evict a nesting Tenant. You wait for spring, or you learn to walk on water.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: And if somebody wanted to go tonight?

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: Then somebody would be arguing with my daughter, not with me.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: Apron's down the steps. She's the wet one.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: You're the flame people. Word came up the stair before you did.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: I've been down at that grate every morning for nineteen days.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: There's a flume behind Lock Five, dry since my father's time. It runs past her.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Past a nesting eel.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: OVER her, technically. Ma's said no nine times, which is how I know it works.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Show us the lock.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Ha! Finally. Down the deep stairs, and mind the third tread, it lies.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: Lock Five held its water flat and green.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: Under the grate, something as long as the chamber shifted its weight and did not look up.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: …She's looking at us.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: She looks at everyone. She's a landlord.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: There. The flume mouth, above the head gates.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Open both gates and the head drops enough to fill it.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: One run, four minutes, out the tailwater below her.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: And the gates?

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Two winches. Ma has the only key to one of them and she sleeps with it. Midnight, then.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Ma will feed you first. She always feeds people before she tells them no.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: Sit. Both of you at the good table, and don't argue, the argument's after.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (The doorframe by the hearth carries a column of pencil marks. They stop, hard, eleven years up.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (There is one drawer in this house with a bright keyhole. Everything else is worn dull.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (That drawer is opened often, and by one person.)

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: Her father drew the north river from memory the night before he went down it.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: He was wrong. That is the whole of the story and I have never once told it shorter.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: …My grandmother kept a rule she never explained either.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: Then you know what they are. They're a wall with a person behind it.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: Night came down the gorge while the plates were still on the table, the way it does in a place with walls that high.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Grid town. Every street named after a number.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (I grew up on a hill where nothing had a name. That is why I do this.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (Somebody should have written it down, so I write everything down.)

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: You never say where you're from.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: Nowhere, yet. It's under survey.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Flame people. Quiet. Ma's asleep and I've got twenty minutes of her being asleep.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Lock Five. Now.

story.ch2.winches._note: TWO-PLAYER PENDING — the shipped beat is a SIX-HAND set piece: two `bothHold` steps (chapter2.js:1474 the left winch, :1506 the seized widow-winch that only turns when Odessa puts her own hands on the bar). Single-body staging: Lake takes the left bar as a companion and Odessa arrives for the widow-winch exactly as authored, so the beat still needs three pairs of hands and the player owns one of them. Restoring co-op is turning the two narrated pulls back into two holds.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Left one first. It's honest.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Both of you on the bar — Lake, you're taller, take the top.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (The left gate came up in six long pulls, and the water changed its mind about which way it was going.)

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Right. Now the widow.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (The second winch did not move. It had not moved in eleven years and it had opinions about tonight.)

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: Move.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: …Ma.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: I said MOVE, girl, you're on my bar.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (Three pairs of hands. The widow-winch turned, complaining, and the head gates of Lock Five stood open at midnight for the first time since her husband drowned.)

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: The flume takes four minutes. Bail with the pumpkin, it's better than it looks.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: Go on, then. Before I remember I said no.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: The Tenant rose alongside as the water took the boat.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: She put one flat eye against the hull, and thought about it.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: Nobody move.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (She sank without hurry. Whatever the inspection had been about, they had passed it.)

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: Then a mile of roaring black at four minutes flat, and no time at all to be frightened in.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: Odessa was on the landing before the sun was. Of course she was.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: She had her lantern, a rope's-end over one shoulder — and a bag.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: …Ma. That's my bag.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: Packed a week ago. You were going north the moment that eel gave you an excuse — I've watched it come the way I watch weather.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: A WEEK? You packed it a week ago and you still said no! Nine times you said no!

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: Ten. And I'd say all ten again.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: The no was what I owed my own heart. The bag is what I owed yours.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: The boat's yours. It was always going to be yours — I only kept the tar on while it waited.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: Mapmaker. A word.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (From inside her coat she takes an oilskin tube, worn glossy at the cap.)

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (She sets it in Vesper's hands, and keeps her own on it a moment longer.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (The drawer. The one bright keyhole. She went home in the dark, then — and stood in front of eleven years, and turned the key.)

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: His chart. The north river — every reach and shoal of it, to the grey marshes.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: He drew it from memory, the night before. It's wrong.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: She'll want to fix it. Don't let her do that alone.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: …I've been correcting a wrong map by myself for eleven years, harbormistress. I don't recommend it to anyone.

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: She won't be alone.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Ma — I'll send word. Every town with a fish-queue between here and wherever—

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: You'll send charts. A chart is a daughter's hand on paper.

lines.speaker: odessa
lines.text: I'll have the charts.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Right — stations! Flame people amidships.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Cat wherever the cat decides. I'm not fighting the cat.

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: (North, then. By water — the lighter warm against my chest, the old road keeping pace up on the rim.)

lines.speaker: lake
lines.text: (Grandmother — the round's gotten strange. But I swear it's still the round.)

lines.speaker: vesper
lines.text: (New page. “Party of three, one boat, one cat. One wrong chart to put right.”)
